page: Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g-3840s is a high-density, general-purpose cloud compute instance designed for demanding transactional and data-intensive applications. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the server features a dedicated AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz across 32 physical cores and 64 threads. The CPU subsystem is equipped with 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core block, accompanied by instruction set extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, AES, and SHA-NI.

System memory is sized at 256.0 GB, adhering to a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The memory bus demonstrates high throughput under benchmark testing, delivering large-block uncached read speeds of 496.98 GB/sec and write speeds of 190.5 GB/sec, placing it in the top tier of evaluated systems. Complementing the compute and RAM is a high-capacity local storage tier consisting of a 3840 GB NVMe SSD. No discrete hardware accelerators are included, and networking provisions include a single complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance metrics indicate strong parallel processing capability. The instance recorded a Geekbench multi-core score of 27795.0 and a single-core score of 2767.0, supported by a software compilation score of 64042.0 using Clang. Extended instruction testing in PassMark reached 107142.77, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression sustained 458.76 GB/sec. Although prompt processing for a 135M parameter language model peaked in the top tier at 4461.42 tokens/sec, text generation token throughput was moderate across smaller models, reflecting typical host CPU execution characteristics without specialized tensor engines.

The qualitative balance of dedicated multi-threaded compute, substantial memory density, and 3.84 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage provides high operational efficiency for mixed deployments. The instance is suited for relational database clusters, Redis caching layers, continuous integration build environments, and large-scale web application deployments requiring low storage latency and sustained CPU availability.
description: Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g-3840s is a dedicated x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. It incorporates 256.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier memory bandwidth reaching 496.98 GB/sec uncached reads, robust compilation metrics, and solid database execution scores. CPU instruction support features AVX-512, BF16, and hardware cryptography. The combination of dense multi-core compute, high memory throughput, and expansive bundled NVMe storage makes this instance technically suited for large transactional databases, multi-threaded build systems, and distributed enterprise application workloads.
